Arizona Cardinals.longComment: Love will miss a fourth consecutive game Sunday but will then be eligible to come off injured reserve ahead of Week 13 against the Eagles. LaFleur previously said Love will be reevaluated Monday once eligible to return, and the coach added Friday that he expects to know more Wednesday once the Cardinals return to practice. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight are still the leading in-house backfield options in the meantime.

Beck has yet to resume practicing and will miss a second consecutive game Sunday due to back spasms, paving the way for Josh Johnson to start against Washington. LaFleur added that a Week 13 return against the Eagles is in play for Beck, who made his first regular-season NFL start in a 34-6 Week 10 loss to the Rams. Beck's practice participation level leading up to that game will provide an indication regarding his potential availability, and LaFleur added that the team will know more about Beck's status "early in the week," per Weinfuss.

Simon is being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's contest. His absence gives the Cardinals less depth at linebacker behind Jack Gibbens, Mack Wilson and Zaven Collins.

Atlanta Falcons.longComment: Dotson hasn't practiced all week, so it wouldn't be surprising if he's ultimately ruled out for Sunday's game against the Vikings once the Falcons release game designations Friday. Zachariah Branch (hamstring) also remained sidelined at Friday's practice, so Olamide Zaccheaus, Beaux Collins and Chris Blair may be Atlanta's only healthy available wide receivers behind Drake London against Minnesota.

Baltimore Ravens.longComment: Hawkins was held out of Wednesday's practice due to a lingering knee injury, which has prevented him from playing in each of the Ravens' last five games. However, a full session Friday could be enough for Hawkins to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.

After logging a limited listing Wednesday, Henry's upgrade to 'full' Thursday has him trending in the right direction as Sunday's game against the Texans approaches. Either way, Friday's final injury report will dictate whether or not the Ravens' lead back carries an injury designation heading into the weekend.

Madubuike was unable to play against the Panthers in Week 11 due to a hamstring injury that he sustained against the Chargers in Week 10. He would need to practice in at least a limited capacity over the next two days to have a realistic shot at playing against the Texans on Sunday.

Buffalo Bills.longComment: Benford will end up missing a second consecutive game due to a groin injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Jets. Maxwell Hairston should see a bump in defensive snaps at outside cornerback in the absence of Benford, whose next chance to play is Week 13 against the Patriots on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Carolina Panthers.longComment: Per Mike Kaye of ESPN.com, McMillan was in a helmet and pads as the Panthers made their way to the practice field Friday but ditched them by the time the team stretched. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will include McMillan's activity level, if any, after he was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's practice estimate due to a sore foot.

Okereke is in danger of missing a third consecutive game as he continues to deal with a knee injury suffered during Week 8. If he ends up being unable to play in Monday's matchup versus the Buccaneers, Tyrel Dodson will likely get another start at inside linebacker.

Evans may have picked up the injury during the Panthers' 35-33 win over the Ravens this past Sunday, when he caught all five of his targets for 44 yards, which included a 23-yard grab in the first quarter. Given that the Panthers didn't practice Thanksgiving Day, Evans' practice participation over the next two days will be worth monitoring ahead of Monday's game against the Buccaneers.

Tremble was cleared to play through a knee injury against the Ravens in Week 11, when he hauled in his lone target for 18 yards while playing 59 of 71 offensive snaps (83.1 percent) in a 35-33 win for the Panthers. Carolina did not practice Thanksgiving Day, so Tremble's participation over the next two days will provide clarity on his status ahead of Monday's NFC South showdown against Tampa Bay.

The Panthers didn't practice Thursday for Thanksgiving, so the report provided by the team was an estimation. Given that, Brooks' practice participation over the next two days will provide a better indication of his status heading into Monday's NFC South tilt against the Buccaneers. However, Brooks would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Week 12. The third-year running back landed on IR in late September after undergoing surgery to repair a core-muscle injury that he sustained against the Falcons in Week 2.

For s second week in a row, Waller is dealing with a knee injury, but his listing to begin this week implies he's a bit healthier after kicking off Week 11 prep with a DNP. He'll have two more opportunities to practice in full Friday and Saturday before the Panthers potentially make a call on his status for Monday's game at Tampa Bay.

Incoom was placed on injured reserve in late October due to a calf injury that he sustained in Week 6 against the Eagles. Regardless of his practice participation over the next three days, the Panthers would have to activate Incoom from injured reserve in order for him to be available for Monday's NFC South tilt against the Buccaneers.

Christensen has been rehabbing from a hamstring injury all year, but he was not activated from IR within 21 days of returning to practice, so he'll now miss the rest of the season. The veteran guard will now have to look forward to hopefully returning at some point in 2027.

Horn is currently considered day-to-day, but head coach Dave Canales wants to ensure Horn is in a great head space before returning. The 2021 first-round pick has been sidelined since late September, while Chau Smith-Wade has handled slot-cornerback duties in his absence. The Panthers will still have to officially activate Horn off injured reserve before he's eligible to return.

Chicago Bears.longComment: Schefter reported earlier that the Bears planned to place Loveland on injured reserve due to the knee injury the TE sustained in Thursday's 39-35 win over the Lions, which would rule Loveland out for at least four weeks. Chicago wants to gather more information before a determination is made on Loveland's status, and the door is still open for a shorter absence, though it would be surprising at this point if he's able to play Dec. 6 against the Jaguars.

Williams seemingly went for a precautionary X-ray after Week 12 action due to a "weird fall" that occurred during Thursday's contest in which he engineered two TD drives in the final 8:20 of the fourth quarter to eke out a four-point victory. He completed 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions and recorded three carries for 15 yards. With plenty of time to recover before the Bears' next game Sunday, Dec. 6 against the Jaguars, Williams has a decent chance to avoid practice restrictions next week.

The cornerback didn't practice at all this week and will miss a second straight game after he was injured in Week 9 against the Bucs. Clark Phillips handled third cornerback duties in last Sunday's win over the Saints.

Johnson injured his ankle in Sunday's win over the Saints, and with the quick turnaround for Week 12, he won't be available against the Lions. The Bears will roll with D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai as their only healthy backs for Thursday's game.

Cincinnati Bengals.longComment: Risner did not play in the Bengals' loss to the Commanders on Monday night due to multiple knee injuries. The starting right guard remains day-to-day with the issue, meaning he could return for Sunday's game against the Saints. If Risner cannot suit up for Week 12, Jalen Rivers is set to start at right guard again.

Davis strung together multiple full practices since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 12, but he still drew the doubtful tag for Monday's game. He'll end up missing a seventh consecutive game due to a hamstring injury, and his next chance to return is Week 12 against the Saints on Sunday.

Iosivas will remain on injured reserve for at least one more week, after the Bengals had listed him as doubtful heading into Monday's contest following a trio of full practices from Thursday through Saturday. If the fourth-year wideout can turn in another full slate of practices in Week 12, he should have a better chance of being restored to the 53-man roster ahead of the Bengals' Nov. 29 matchup with the Saints.

Burks has been working through a groin issue for the past couple of weeks, and he aggravated the injury during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. His placement on IR means he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 20.

Cleveland Browns.longComment: Coach Todd Monken noted Friday that the team pushed Boston (who was deemed a 'DNP' at practice over the last few days) pretty hard earlier in the week, then pulled back a little bit, while adding that the Browns should have a better idea regarding the wide receiver's Week 12 status Saturday. If Boston ends up out or limited this weekend, Malachi Corley, Tylan Wallace and Isaiah Bond would be in line to see added opportunities behind KC Concepcion and Jerry Jeudy.

Sanders was designated to return from injured reserve Tuesday, and he would need to be added to the active roster with an official transaction prior to Sunday's game to have a chance to play. Even if Sanders gets the green light, he's unlikely to see much action on offense, with Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson and Jaleel McLaughlin all healthy in Cleveland's backfield.

Williams may have picked up the injury during the Browns' Week 10 win over the Texans, when he logged nine tackles (five solo) and one pass defense. The injury designation follows the Browns' Week 11 bye, and he'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation ahead of Sunday's game against Las Vegas.

The Browns are coming out of a bye, so it's unclear whether McGuire picked up the injury during the Browns' Week 10 win over the Texans. Regardless, he'll have two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.

Hickman was held out of the Browns' Week 10 win over the Texans while in the league's concussion protocol. Cleveland's Week 11 bye gave him extra time to recover, and while his full session Wednesday is encouraging, Hickman would need to pass an evaluation by an independent neurologist in order to clear protocol and be available to play Sunday against Las Vegas.

Dallas Cowboys.longComment: Williams recorded four tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, before leaving late in the fourth quarter due to back spasms. He was not cleared to return to Thursday's game, but there doesn't appear to be much concern over his status for Week 13 given the extra rest that Dallas will have.

Moore strung together three consecutive full practices during Week 12 prep, but he would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Thanksgiving Day. The rookie fourth-rounder has yet to make his 2026 regular-season debut due to a hip injury that he picked up in training camp.

Locke entered the league's concussion protocol following the Cowboys' Week 9 win over the Colts. He hasn't progressed enough in his recovery to return for Thanksgiving Day and will thus miss a third consecutive game. Locke's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Seahawks on Monday, Dec. 7.

Mingo's absence for Thanksgiving Day will be his third missed game in a row due to an ankle injury that he sustained in Week 9 against the Colts. His absence means KaVontae Turpin and Camden Brown will continue to operate in rotational roles on offense behind CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy. Mingo's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Seahawks on Monday, Dec. 7.

Bland was placed on injured reserve Sunday after suffering an ankle injury during the Week 10 loss to the 49ers, but the injury is not expected to be season-ending. The earliest Bland will be eligible to make his return is the Week 16 matchup versus Jacksonville, and Ameer Speed and Cobie Durant should continue to see increased playing time in his absence.

Denver Broncos.longComment: Jones had previously been ruled out for Friday's matchup versus the Steelers but will now be forced to miss at least four games before he's eligible to return. In his absence, Tyler Onyedim should be in line for increased playing time.

Lohner was a full participant in all three practice sessions during Week 12 prep. However, the second-year pro is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve, so his next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6. Lohner is in the final stages of his recovery from a procedure on his foot in June.

Tuesday was Denver's first practice, and given Elliss's absence, he's highly unlikely to participate in any of the Broncos' next two sessions ahead of Black Friday. The third-year linebacker is recovering from an ankle injury that landed him on IR in late October. Assuming he doesn't play in Week 12, Elliss's next opportunity to play would be Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Detroit Lions.longComment: Wonnum was able to practice in a limited capacity Wednesday, but that didn't end up being enough for him to suit up Thursday. He leads the Lions with 7.0 sacks this season, so the veteran defensive end's absence is a big deal for Detroit. Tyler Lacy, Ahmed Hassanein, Eric O'Neill and Anthony Lucas could all be involved in trying to fill the void left by Wonnum's absence Thursday.

Clark dealt with a hamstring issue during Week 12 prep and is going to miss his first game of the campaign as a result. He's been a starter at safety for the Lions all season and played every defensive snap in three of Detroit's past four games. Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch will start at safety Thursday, with Andre Cisco working in reserve.

Gill-Howard suffered a season-ending knee injury during the Lions' Week 11 win over the Buccaneers. The rookie sixth-rounder will finish his first NFL campaign with 11 tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks, across 10 regular-season games.

Green Bay Packers.longComment: Prior to leaving, the linebacker recorded four tackles (two solo). Dani Dennis-Sutton and Brenton Cox will see an uptick in snaps off the edge for Green Bay.

The wideout hasn't cleared concussion checks and will miss the remainder of the Week 12 contest after he was injured at the end of the second quarter when Watson took a hit to the head from Kamren Kinchens. Look for J. Michael Sturdivant and Bo Melton to see increased snaps alongside Matthew Golden and Savion Williams with Watson sidelined.

Franklin drew the questionable tag for Wednesday's game following three consecutive limited practices. However, the veteran linebacker will end up missing a fifth consecutive game due to a hairline fracture in his shin that he suffered during a practice session in late October, so Ty'Ron Hopper will continue to operate in an elevated role on defense. Franklin's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Coming out of the Packers' Week 11 bye, head coach Matt LaFleur told Matt Schneidman of The Athletic on Saturday that he didn't expect Jacobs to play in Week 12, but he also gave the running back a "chance to prove" he can. Jacobs then was listed as limited on practice reports Sunday through Tuesday and tagged as questionable ahead of Wednesday's game. Such activity wasn't enough for Jacobs to get the all clear to suit up, meaning Green Bay's backfield will be manned by Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks for a second consecutive contest.

LaFleur acknowledged that Musgrove is still in the process of rehabbing the neck injury he sustained during OTAs in June, and the Packers haven't yet prepared for the tight end to resume practicing. Barring dramatic progress in his recovery over the next month, Musgrave looks like he'll be sidelined for the final season of his rookie deal before hitting free agency in the spring.

Houston Texans.longComment: Wilson adds that Boutte isn't expected to play Sunday against the Ravens, and while things are certainly trending that way based on Boutte's inability to practice all week, that notion has yet to be confirmed by an official team source. Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and Marvin Harrison will compete for playing time and targets alongside Nico Collins if Boutte is ruled out.

Schultz wasn't listed on Wednesday's injury report, which indicates that the illness is a new concern for the veteran tight end. A full session Friday would likely be enough for him to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Ravens. Brevin Jordan (finger/foot), Foster Moreau and Marlin Klein would all be in line for larger roles on offense in the event that Schultz is not cleared to play in Week 12.

Rankins sustained an ankle injury during Thursday's win over the Colts and did not return to the contest. The defensive tackle's absence from Wednesday's session suggests the injury was significant. Rankins will have Thursday and Friday's sessions to return to practice in time to avoid an injury designation, or to at least have a chance to suit up for Sunday's game against the Ravens.

Hunter did not play in Thursday's win over the Colts due to his hamstring injury. The defensive end has still not returned to practice since sustaining the injury during Week 10 prep. If Hunter continues to miss practice, he will be in line to miss his third consecutive game due to the injury.

Marks didn't practice last week before being ruled out for this past Thursday's 26-3 win over the Colts, but with some extra recovery time since then, the running back is trending toward a return to the lineup Sunday against the Ravens. To get there, however, he'll need to fully progress through the NFL's concussion protocol in the days leading up to the Texans' Week 12 contest.

The Texans announced Rutledge's injury in the waning moments of the contest, but he had been in the medical tent well before that time. Febechi Nwaiwu took over at left guard following Rutledge's departure. With Houston not set to play again until Sunday, Nov. 29, against Baltimore, Rutledge will look to recover from the stinger in time to suit up.

Indianapolis Colts.longComment: DJ Giddens is set to inherit change-of-pace duties behind Jonathan Taylor in McGowan's absence. McGowan, who injured his hamstring in the Week 11 loss to the Texans, will have a bye to heal before possibly returning against the Eagles in Week 14.

Curry was placed on the Colts' injured reserve Tuesday, and head coach Shane Steichen informed reporters Wednesday that the rookie sixth-rounder's wrist injury was severe enough for him to require season-ending surgery. Curry will end his first NFL campaign with 26 tackles (14 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two fumble recoveries across 11 regular-season games. His absence means Carl Lawson, Jaylahn Tuimoloau and George Gumbs are all in line for more rotational snaps at defensive end.

Taylor-Britt was a full participant in Wednesday's practice in what was his first session since suffering a groin injury in Week 7 against the Vikings. Even if he strings together two more full sessions, Taylor-Britt would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Giants.

Additionally, Pierce acknowledged that playing in Week 1 was a bit lofty, per Bowen, with the WR saying Wednesday that he was still managing some pain at that stage. In any case, Pierce indicated that he's confident that his current recovery plan will lead to a full return to health. When that will be remains to be seen, but the 2022 second-rounder is still on IR ahead of Week 12, with the Colts presumably not planning to rush him back given the team's 3-8 record in a campaign that's been marked by the team moving several key players ahead of the trade deadline.

Jacksonville Jaguars.longComment: If Tuten's absence Friday is confirmed by the team's injury report, that would mark a third consecutive 'DNP' for Jacksonville's starting running back. Coach Liam Coen intimated earlier Friday that Tuten's participation level Friday would factor into Tuten's potential availability for Sunday's game against the Titans, so Tuten appears more likely than not to sit out Sunday based on this latest development. If Tuten is ruled out, Chris Rodriguez would be in line to lead a backfield that also includes LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah.

Washington was added to Jacksonville's injury report Thursday due to a shoulder injury, and the impact of the injury has escalated from limiting his practice participation Thursday to sidelining Jacksonville's top receiver Sunday and possibly beyond then. In Washington's absence, Jakobi Meyers (ankle), Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and possibly Travis Hunter or CJ Williams -- to a lesser degree -- could garner more attention from Trevor Lawrence against a Titans secondary that has allowed the most catches and yards per game in the league to wide receivers. Additional details regarding Washington's injury should emerge before the Jaguars travel to Chicago in Week 13.

Mekari now has a 21-day window for the Jaguars to return him to the active roster. The right guard returned to practice as a limited participant. If Mekari can upgrade to a full participant by Friday's session, there is a chance he could be activated for Sunday's game against the Titans. The Jaguars could just as easily take it slow with the veteran offensive lineman to ensure he is healthy and ready for his return to the field, so Ezra Cleveland may be in line for another start at right guard.

Dating back to Week 8, Meyers has been listed on Jaguars injury reports with the ankle issue, but it hasn't stopped him from being available on game days. His limitations Wednesday were most likely maintenance-related after he turned in one his best performances of 2026 in this past Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants. Meyers played 83 percent of the offensive snaps in the loss, finishing with four catches for a season-high 85 yards on 10 targets.

Kansas City Chiefs.longComment: Smith was injured in the fourth quarter of Week 12 action, but the Chiefs never announced the reason for him hitting the sideline until Reid spoke to the media afterward. If the severity of Smith's issue is enough to require an absence or more time off, Hunter Nourzad is the likely candidate to man right guard for Kansas City.

Royals left the game in the third quarter and was ruled out not long afterward due to an ankle injury. The severity of the sprain will determine if Royals is in danger of missing any time. If that comes to pass for Royals, Andrew Armstrong likely will be on track for a few more offensive snaps behind Rashee Rice, Josh Downs, Xavier Worthy and Cyrus Allen.

Despite logging full participation sessions in Week 12 prep, Norman-Lott will not suit up for Thursday night's contest. The Chiefs activated the defensive tackle from the reserve/PUP list Nov. 18, but he is not quite ready to return to the field.
Moore will miss his third consecutive game with an ankle injury. Joshua Ezeudu will once again be called upon to start at right tackle for the Chiefs' offense.

VanSumeren didn't practice Tuesday due to a sprained knee that will now keep him out for at least the next four weeks, according to Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site. In six regular-season games in 2026, the fourth-year pro played a majority of his reps on special teams, with just six of 104 total snaps coming on offense.

Las Vegas Raiders.longComment: Hemingway is still battling the shoulder injury that sidelined him for the Week 11 loss to Denver. The 25-year-old will likely need to be upgraded to a full participant in Friday's practice in order to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's matchup against the Browns.

The star tight end, who was inactive this past Sunday against the Broncos, now has strung together four straight limited practices, which bodes well for his chances of being back for this weekend's game against the Browns. Friday's final injury report will determine whether Bowers carries an injury designation for the contest or is fully cleared for Week 12 action.

Butler enterted the NFL's concussion protocol after being ruled out for the remainder of the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos. The defensive tackle will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to full-contact practice.

Johnson was a full participant in Wednesday's practice in what was his first on-field action since being placed on injured reserve in late October due to a neck injury. His ability to practice in full is an encouraging sign, but Johnson would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Browns.

Keenan went down with a knee injury in the first half, and he will now officially be sidelined for the rest of Week 11. With Adam Butler (concussion) also done for the day, JJ Pegues will handle the bulk of the workload at defensive tackle versus the Broncos.

Los Angeles Chargers.longComment: Njoku also was deemed a 'DNP' on Wednesday, so the tight end presumably will need to practice Friday, in some capacity, in order to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Patriots. If Njoku ends up sidelined this weekend, Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will be in line to lead the Chargers' Week 12 TE corps.

Herbert, who landed in the NFL's concussion protocol in the wake of this past Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets, didn't practice Wednesday, either. He thus is looking iffy, at best, for this weekend's game against the Patriots, especially given the Chargers' 1-9 record. If Herbert is inactive versus New England, DJ Uiagalelei would be in line to start at QB in his place, with Jake Browning available to back him up.

It's not clear when Leonard was injured, as he logged a season-high 70 percent defensive snap share against the Jets last Sunday. Regardless, he's now required to miss at least four games while on IR. Avery Smith and Isas Waxter may get more opportunities in the secondary during Leonard's absence.

The rookie first-rounder is working through an ankle injury that he picked up during the first half of the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets in Week 12. Mesidor has two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's contest against the Patriots.

Tuipulotu appears to have sustained his ankle injury in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets. The outside linebacker will need to upgrade his practice participation in Thursday or Friday's session for a chance to suit up for Sunday's contest against the Patriots. If the 24-year-old must miss the game, Akheem Mesidor (ankle) or Caleb Murphy will likely start opposite Khalil Mack.

Thompson has not played since the Chargers' Week 2 game with the Raiders. The wide receiver initially dealt with a quadriceps injury before sustaining a hamstring injury while still recovering. Thompson's long string of DNPs continues into Week 12 prep, and it appears there may be no end in sight.

Tomlinson likely sustained his knee injury in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets. The defensive tackle will likely need to return to practice by Friday's session for a chance to suit up for Sunday's game against the Patriots.

Still did not play in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets due to an ankle injury he sustained in Friday's practice. The cornerback remains sidelined with the issue, leaving Deane Leonard and Genesis Smith as the early options at slot cornerback for Sunday's game against the Patriots.

Henley did not play in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets due to his knee injury. The linebacker has not practiced since sustaining the injury after Week 10. If Henley cannot suit up for Sunday's game, Marlowe Wax and Troy Dye will likely see increased snap shares at inside linebacker next to Del'Shawn Phillips.

The running back was injured in last Sunday's loss to the Jets. If Mitchell needs to miss time, it would likely turn this frustrating three-way committee backfield into a more traditional two-man affair, with Omarion Hampton handling early-down work and Kimani Vidal spelling him in passing situations.

Los Angeles Rams.longComment: Murray limped to the locker room early in the fourth quarter and never returned. Head coach Sean McVay didn't mention Murray's status following the win, but it sounds like he may be dealing with a more-than-minor injury. That would further deplete a Los Angeles offensive line that has been without starting left guard Steve Avila (hamstring) since he was hurt Week 9.

With Higbee forced out during the contest after Davis Allen (ankle) was injured earlier in the game, the Rams have only two healthy tight ends left. Colby Parkinson and Max Klare will play virtually every offensive snap the rest of the way for Los Angeles. Prior to leaving, Higbee caught one of three targets for 14 yards.

Ferguson initially seemed to be making good progress in his recovery from the ankle injury, as the Rams elected to open his 21-day evaluation window Nov. 4. However, Ferguson's activation from IR was delayed after he strained his hamstring shortly after he resumed working out, and he hasn't practiced in more than two weeks. Rather than the hamstring issue, McVay noted that the ankle injury remained the greater concern for Ferguson, who didn't improve as well as the Rams had hoped and now will require a procedure. Los Angeles will have to proceed without two of its top pass catchers for the remainder of the season, as Puka Nacua recently underwent an MCL surgery that entails an estimated 4-to-5-month recovery timeline.

Miami Dolphins.longComment: Wayne has missed the Dolphins' last two games due to a quadriceps injury. He would need to practice in at least a limited capacity over the next two days to have a realistic chance of being available for Sunday's game against the Jets.
Harrison suffered a hamstring injury in Week 1 that landed him on injured reserve. The fact the Dolphins opted to open his practice window after nine weeks suggests Harrison may be nearing a return.

That said, per Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com, Hafley added that the Dolphins will evaluate the QB's status again depending on how he feels at the end of his minimum required stay on IR. For now, Willis is out for at least three more games, with Kyle McCord currently filling in as 1-9 Miami's starting signal-caller.

Minnesota Vikings.longComment: Smith is working through a thigh injury that he likely picked up during the Vikings' Week 11 loss to the 49ers. He was listed as a DNP on Wednesday's estimated report, so his ability to practice in a limited capacity Thursday indicates that he is progressing in his recovery, and a full session Friday could be enough for him to avoid a designation ahead of Sunday's game against Atlanta.

Price has been limited in each of the first two practices of Week 12 prep due to knee and groin injuries that he likely sustained during the Vikings' 35-10 loss to the 49ers in Week 11. A full practice Friday would presumably be enough for Price to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Falcons. He has a 6-75-1 receiving line on as many targets over his last two outings while operating in an expanded role on offense in the absence of Jordan Addison (thumb), the latter of whom is unlikely to play against Atlanta.

Murray appears to be drawing closer to being active for the first time since Week 8, but he may need to practice fully Friday in order to avoid a designation ahead of Sunday's contest against the Falcons. He's missed the last three games due to a Grade 2 hamstring strain, and he likely will slot in as Kirk Cousins' direct backup once the former is healthy enough to suit up.

Addison's next listing on an injury report that isn't a DNP will be his first since Nov. 13, when he suffered a thumb injury that required surgery and so far has sidelined him for two games. Head coach Kevin O'Connell relayed to Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune on Monday that Addison is "progressing well" in his recovery but is unlikely to play Sunday against the Falcons. Ultimately, Addison's status for Week 12 may be clarified once the Vikings post Friday's practice report.

Rodgers was unable to play against the 49ers in Week 11 due to a quadriceps injury. He hasn't been cleared to practice since picking up the injury during last Thursday's session, and he'll have two more chances to return to practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Falcons.

New England Patriots.longComment: Doubs was designated to return from injured reserve earlier in the week, but Vrabel's comments suggest the wide receiver isn't on track to be activated ahead of Sunday's contest. If Doubs remains sidelined, Sunday would mark his fifth consecutive absence. QB Drake Maye (lower leg) and WR A.J. Brown (hamstring) have both been officially ruled out while Doubs' inactive status has yet to be confirmed.

With Brown unavailable following the Patriots' Week 11 bye, Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams are in line to handle the team's WR duties in Tommy DeVito's first regular-season start at QB. Meanwhile, Romeo Doubs (shoulder) isn't likely to be activated from IR this weekend, so it looks like the earliest either of New England's top two wideouts could be available is Dec. 6 against the Bills.

Rouse is in the league's concussion protocol, which prevented him from playing in Week 10 against the Lions in Munich. Despite the extra rest courtesy of the Week 11 bye, the third-year pro has not progressed enough in his recovery to return to practice. Even if he practices over the coming days, an independent neurologist would need to clear Rouse from protocol in order for him to be available for Sunday's game against the Chargers.

The move opens Vera-Tucker's 21-day practice window. The oft-injured offensive lineman went down in the Patriots' Week 6 win over the Jets. Greg Van Roten started New England's last game at left guard.

Per Reiss, teams are limited to eight players that can be designated to return from the list over the course of the regular season, and the Patriots are close to using them all. "Right now, he's not on injured reserve," Vrabel said Monday. "He's on the active roster, so that's where it is today. I think that those things are obviously fluid. But we want to try to give him every opportunity that we can to be back at some point in time. I don't know when that will be; I'm not sure. But also, try to manage the roster and do what we need to do to try to win each week." On Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Maye was on track to miss at least six weeks, a timetable that suggests, in a best-case scenario, the QB could make a push for a late-season return or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Heading into a Week 12 game against the Chargers, Tommy DeVito is slated to work as the team's starter, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup. Additionally, there's the possibility that the team considers Daniel Jones -- who the Colts let go Friday -- as an alternative, but Vrabel told Reiss that in the short term at least, adding another signal-caller is not something that's being planned.

Jones left the game during the fourth quarter, and given the score of the contest, the veteran linebacker is unlikely to return to Sunday's game. If that's the case, then Jones will finish with two tackles (one solo) and one QB hit.

New Orleans Saints.longComment: Per Ross Jackson of WWL-TV, Johnson -- who logged a 'DNP' on Wednesday's practice estimate -- wasn't spotted at Thursday's session. The tight end thus has one more chance to practice before the Saints' Week 12 injury designations are assigned. If Johnson ends up limited or out this weekend, Noah Fant and Oscar Delp would be in line for added snaps in the team's offense this weekendi.

Emerson was held out of practice during Week 11 prep and did not play against the Bears this past Sunday. His full practice participation indicates that he's progressing through the league's concussion protocol, but he would need to pass an evaluation by an independent neurologist in order to be available for Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.

Werner was held out of the Saints' Week 11 loss to the Bears due to a hamstring injury that he sustained against the Panthers in Week 10. Wednesday was his first practice participation since the injury, and he'll have two more opportunities to log a full session and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Bengals.

New York Giants.longComment: Carter was a DNP for Wednesday's session due to a calf issue, and the second-year edge rusher is now battling through an illness. His lack of practice reps are concerning, but he has one more opportunity to log at least a limited session ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts. Trace Ford and Dawuane Smoot would both be in line for more defensive snaps in the event that Carter is not cleared to play against Indianapolis.

Likely suffered a strained groin last Friday, and while it didn't stop him from suiting up for this past Sunday's win against the Jaguars, he gathered in just one of three targets for 35 yards on a 76 percent snap share. He now has managed back-to-back limited listings to begin Week 12 prep, and Friday's practice report will reveal if he has a designation for Sunday's contest at Indianapolis.

Phillips appears to have come down with an illness, taking him out of Wednesday's prep session. The cornerback has two Week 12 practices remaining to be a healthy participant before he would have an injury designation heading into Sunday's game against the Colts.

Reese likely sustained his back injury in the Giants' Week 11 win over the Jaguars. The linebacker not missing a practice session with the injury is a good sign, but he will likely need to continue stringing sessions together Thursday and Friday to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts.

Newsome is expected to undergo surgery for a sprained ankle that he sustained in the Giants' 23-18 win over the Jaguars on Sunday. Now that he's on IR, Newsome will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Lions on Monday, Dec. 28. Paulson Adebo is expected to start opposite Deonte Banks at outside cornerback in Newsome's absence.

New York Jets.longComment: Cooper will miss a second consecutive game Sunday, bringing him up to six total absences as a result of ankle injuries during his rookie campaign. Adonai Mitchell is set to start on the outside opposite Garrett Wilson, with Isaiah Williams manning the slot, though another elevation for practice-squad WR Sterling Shepard could be on the table after Shepard scored twice in the Week 11 win over the Chargers. Cooper's next chance to play will be a Week 14 home game against the Broncos following the Jets' Week 13 bye.

Phillips was listed as limited for the second consecutive day despite managing to play through the ankle injury during the Week 11 win over the Chargers. Jack Heflin would be in line for increased playing time during Sunday's matchup against the Dolphins if Phillips ends up being unable to play.

Onyemata was designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 18 but was not cleared to play against the Chargers in Week 11. If he can string together full practices over the next two days, then Onyemata would have a good chance of being activated from IR ahead of Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Dolphins.
The defensive lineman was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. Sweat hasn't played since Week 7 and has logged 17 tackles (five solo) across 229 defensive snaps this season.

Philadelphia Eagles.longComment: Smith put together a career stat line during the Eagles' Thanksgiving Day win, with the veteran wide receiver hauling in 11 of 14 targets for 200 yards and two touchdowns. He was in and out of the game after landing hard on his tailbone on one of his targets in the fourth quarter and was in noticeable pain when on the field. Smith will have additional time to rest courtesy of the Thursday game, but his status over the coming days will be worth monitoring ahead of the Eagles' Week 13 road tilt against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Goedert injured his right shoulder during the first half of Thursday's game and was not cleared to return. He'll undergo further tests to determine the severity of the injury, but the veteran tight end is certainly in jeopardy of not being available for the Eagles' Week 13 road tilt against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6. Johnny Mundt, Zach Ertz and rookie second-rounder Eli Stowers would all be in line for larger roles on offense if Goedert were to miss time.
Hall exited the game in the second half, casting doubt on his availability for the remainder of the contest. Ty Robinson could see an uptick in playing time if Hall ends up being unable to return.
Epps is done for the day after suffering a foot injury in the third quarter. In his absence, Kenny Moore has taken over at safety.

This marks Barkley's second diagnosed stinger of the campaign, but on the previous occasion in Week 2 against the Titans, he was able to check back in to the contest. The Eagles may opt to exercise caution with Barkley, however, because he tended to a neck issue on a short week following this past Sunday's win against the Steelers.

DeJean was shaken up on the Eagles' first defensive drive of the first quarter and was taken to the locker room, where medical staff diagnosed the third-year defensive back with a concussion. Michael Carter should see more defensive snaps in the secondary in the absence of DeJean, who will now work through the league's protocol in an effort to be available for Week 13 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6.

After his trade to the Bengals fell through two weeks ago, Ebiketie is now dealing with an injury that will sideline him for at least one contest. Jalyx Hunt and A.J. Epenesa should soak up extra snaps off the edge for the Eagles.

The cornerback was injured in last Sunday's win over the Steelers. With Jones set to miss Thanksgiving Day against Dallas, Riq Woolen and Kelee Ringo are likely to see increased snaps opposite Quinyon Mitchell.

Pittsburgh Steelers.longComment: Holcomb popped up on the injury report Thursday, leaving his status for Friday's matchup up in the air. Carson Bruener and Jacoby Windmon should be in line for increased playing time if Holcomb ends up being unable to play.

Dunker managed to return to practice for the first time since suffering a knee injury in September but will have to wait at least another week before making his return. The rookie sixth-round pick should provide additional depth at guard once healthy.

Highsmith was held out of practice all week due to an ankle injury that he picked up during the Steelers' 19-16 loss to the Eagles this past Sunday, when he logged 2.0 sacks and forced a fumble before his exit. Nick Herbig and Jack Sawyer are the top candidates to start opposite T.J. Watt at the edge rusher position in the absence of Highsmith, whose next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Texans on Sunday, Dec. 6.

Skowronek has been working through a calf issue since mid-October, and he appeared to aggravate the injury during the Steelers' Week 11 loss to the Eagles. Now that he's on injured reserve, Skowronek will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 27. Max Hurleman was signed off the practice squad to the 53-man roster in a corresponding move.

San Francisco 49ers.longComment: The 49ers didn't hold a practice for Thanksgiving Day, but Watkins has been listed as a non-participant for the first two sessions of Week 12 prep due to a groin injury. He has one more opportunity to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks. In the event that Watkins is not cleared to play against Seattle, more offensive snaps would be available for the likes of Jacob Cowing, Keenan Allen and Demarcus Robinson.

After not practicing Wednesday, Evans' upgrade in listing one day later generally is a good sign that he has a chance to suit up Sunday versus the Seahawks. In his return from a three-game absence this past Sunday against the Vikings in Mexico City, he logged just 43 percent of the snaps but reeled off six catches (on seven targets) for 109 yards and one touchdown.

Purdy has kicked off Week 12 prep with back-to-back DNPs due to an ankle injury, giving him just one more chance to mix into drills Friday before the 49ers potentially tag him with a designation for Sunday's showdown with the Seahawks. There's been no indication that Purdy is in danger of missing that contest, but if it comes to pass, Mac Jones is available to start under center.

Pleasants opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a knee injury that he sustained in a preseason game against the Chargers in late August. He was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and he would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Seahawks. With Colton McKivitz (ankle) out for the rest of the season, Pleasants would be a candidate to start at right tackle once he's removed from IR.

McKivitz was diagnosed with a fractured and dislocated ankle that he sustained in the 49ers' Week 11 win over the Vikings. He's expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season, and Vederian Lowe is expected to take over as the starter at right tackle in McKivitz's absence.

Lenoir has been playing through a foot injury since Week 9 against the Raiders, so it's not surprising to see his practice reps limited Wednesday. Unless he suffers a setback, Lenoir should be available for Sunday's NFC West tilt against the Seahawks.

Greenlaw was not cleared by medical staff to play against the Vikings in Week 11 due to a neck issue. He's opened Week 12 prep with a limited practice, and a full session over the next two days would likely be enough for him to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

Okuayinonu suffered a broken foot in practice ahead of Week 1 and required surgery. He appears to be making progress and could return at some point before the end of the regular season. The 28-year-old appeared in 15 regular-season games last season, and made 12 starts and recorded 23 tackles (16 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and a forced fumble.

Stribling was diagnosed with a deltoid sprain of his left ankle after getting injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and underwent surgery Sept. 16. The 23-year-old was handed an estimated recovery timeline of about 10 weeks, leaving the 49ers optimistic that he would be ready to play at some point in December. While Shanahan indicated that Stribling's timeline doesn't appear to have changed, the young wideout will need to get back on the practice field before the 49ers can hone in on a more precise target date for him to resume playing. Given the haziness of his return date along with the fact that he could face limitations with his snaps once activated, Stribling likely isn't worth holding in redraft leagues at this point in the season.

Seattle Seahawks.longComment: Bradford was listed as limited for the second consecutive day as he continues to deal with a knee injury. The 2023 fourth-round pick should continue to serve as the team's backup right guard behind Grey Zabel during Sunday's matchup against the 49ers.

Lock has been working through an elbow issue to his throwing arm since late October, which has limited his participation in the first two practices of Week 12 prep. He started in each of the Seahawks' two games prior to the Week 11 bye, but is expected to revert to backup duties provided Sam Darnold (quadriceps) is cleared to start against the 49ers on Sunday. If Lock isn't available to play against San Francisco, then Jalen Milroe (illness) would be in line to operate as Seattle's QB2 behind Darnold.

An ankle injury has left Smith-Njigba listed as limited on both of the Seahawks' Week 12 practice reports so far, meaning he has just one more chance to get back to full Friday, at which point the Seahawks may tag him with a designation for Sunday's game at San Francisco. Through 10 contests this season, he's failed to reach the century mark in receiving yards just two times and also has 10 touchdown catches.

It is unclear where Jones picked up his knee injury, but it still appears to be bothering the linebacker after the Seahawks' Week 11 bye. Jones will have Thursday and Friday's practice sessions to upgrade to full participation and avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's divisional contest against the 49ers.

Nelson underwent a minor procedure on his knee in early November and will be sidelined for a second consecutive game. He's had additional time to rest thanks to the Seahawks' Week 11 bye, and Macdonald relayed Wednesday that the team is "hopeful" that Nelson will be cleared to return for Week 13 against the Cowboys on Monday, Dec. 7. Greg Zabel will likely start at left guard in Nelson's absence.

Per John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site, head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters Wednesday that Lucas is not a candidate for injured reserve but is expected to miss "days to weeks" due to an ankle sprain that he suffered in Week 10 against the Raiders. Josh Jones, Bobby Hart and Chase Lundt are all candidates to start at right tackle for as long as Lucas is sidelined.

Holani was knocked out of the Seahawks' last game in Week 10 at Las Vegas due to a knee injury that eventually was deemed to be an MCL sprain. Per Brady Henderson of ESPN.com, head coach Mike Macdonald said he was uncertain if Holani will require surgery, but the running back will be sidelined for at least four games by virtue of landing on IR. In the meantime, Emanuel Wilson will serve as the team's No. 3 back behind Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price.

Reed limped off the field during the first half and was subsequently deemed doubtful to return. Brandon Pili should get a lot more defensive snaps in the likely scenario that Reed is unable to re-enter Sunday's contest.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers.longComment: Parrish is still dealing with the back injury that he suffered in the Week 11 loss to the Lions. The 22-year-old will likely need to be upgraded to a full participant by Saturday's practice to avoid carrying an injury designation into Monday's matchup against the Panthers.

Winfield is still dealing with the ankle injury that he suffered during the Week 9 loss to the Bears. If he is unable to participate at some point over the next two days of practice, the 2020 second-round pick could be in danger of missing a second consecutive game

Trotter popped up on the injury report Thursday, casting doubt on his availability for Monday's matchup against the Panthers. If the rookie second-round pick ends up being unable to play, SirVocea Dennis would likely start at inside linebacker alongside Alex Anzalone.

McMillan has missed the Buccaneers' last seven games while recovering from an MCL sprain in his left knee that he sustained against the Vikings in Week 3. He was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, and even if he practices in full over the next two days, he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Monday's game against the Panthers.

Rozeboom has been on injured reserve for the Buccaneers' last four games while recovering from a finger injury that he sustained in late October. Tampa Bay's first practice of Week 12 prep is Thursday, so Rozeboom's participation over those three sessions will determine whether he's recovered enough to be activated from IR ahead of Monday's game against the Panthers.

Simmons played 17 defensive snaps in Sunday's loss but did not appear in the box score. The defensive tackle has now entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to full-contact football activities.

Both Morrison and Jacob Parrish (back) were injured in Sunday's loss to Detroit, forcing Tampa Bay to dip into its cornerback depth. Kevin Knowles picked up the extra snaps opposing Zyon McCollum, with Keionte Scott covering the slot.

Washington Commanders.longComment: Burks has been listed on Commanders practice reports with a foot injury since Week 8, but he's missed only one contest (Week 9 against the Rams) in four chances during that span. Friday's report will determine if Burks has a designation ahead of Sunday's contest at Arizona.

Robertson was unable to play against the Bengals on Monday due to an ankle injury that he picked up during Friday's practice. He would need to log a limited session over the next two days to have a chance at playing against the Cardinals on Sunday.

Tunsil underwent surgery in August to repair a torn triceps. The left tackle continues to recover, but he likely will not suit up for the Commanders in 2026 unless the team makes a playoff run. Even then, it remains unclear whether Tunsil would be able to return at all before the 2027 season.
